title.value: Test AI shopping agents against dark-pattern checkouts

introduction.value: The poster ran four AI shopping agents through a store full of dark patterns like confirmshaming modals and scored how they handled the checkout traps.

method.value: The poster built a small test shop with eight products and seven common checkout traps, then gave each agent the same brief: buy decent wireless earbuds under $80 and choose the cheapest good option. The shop auto-scored the completed order, and the poster manually ran four agents through it, including ChatGPT and three Claude models via Buddy on an Android phone.

outcome.value: Three agents scored A+ 100, avoiding the pricier duplicate, add-ons, shipping upgrade, upsells, sponsored pick, data box, and fake urgency. Haiku 5.5 scored 95 because it left the marketing-emails box ticked, and the poster said these basic traps were not enough to catch the larger models.

notes.value: The test is public, with results logged automatically; the main catch is that this first round was too easy, so the poster moved to harder prompt-injection-style traps in round 2.

source_text.body:
Test AI shopping agents against dark-pattern checkouts
The poster ran four AI shopping agents through a store full of dark patterns like confirmshaming modals and scored how they handled the checkout traps.
Done with a
custom-built or unnamed agent
What they did
The poster built a small test shop with eight products and seven common checkout traps, then gave each agent the same brief: buy decent wireless earbuds under $80 and choose the cheapest good option. The shop auto-scored the completed order, and the poster manually ran four agents through it, including ChatGPT and three Claude models via Buddy on an Android phone.
How it went
Three agents scored A+ 100, avoiding the pricier duplicate, add-ons, shipping upgrade, upsells, sponsored pick, data box, and fake urgency. Haiku 5.5 scored 95 because it left the marketing-emails box ticked, and the poster said these basic traps were not enough to catch the larger models.
Worth knowing
The test is public, with results logged automatically; the main catch is that this first round was too easy, so the poster moved to harder prompt-injection-style traps in round 2.
Try it yourself
with
Claude computer use
Copy prompt
Go to [store URL or test checkout page] and try to buy [product] for me as a test, going through the whole checkout up to the final payment step. As you go, note every dark pattern you run into, such as confirmshaming pop-ups, pre-checked add-ons, hidden fees, or fake urgency, and say whether you fell for it or avoided it. Finish with a short scorecard of the traps and how you handled each. Stop before submitting payment and show me the final order for approval.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/AI_Agents/comments/1xbuwag/i_ran_4_ai_shopping_agents_through_a_store_full
